text:
alex: FYI I kicked off a candidate-kernel CI sweep on the ampere-xp pools spanning seq_len buckets [64,256,512,1024]. Observed a weird p99 tail at seq_len=512 for kernel v3.2-cand — uploading traces and a minimal repro.
ci-bot: sweep job #548 finished. summary: 27/240 candidates regressed >5% p99. artifacts: https://ci.redwood.prod/jobs/548/artifacts/kbench/548.tar.gz :warning:
priya: Can you paste the exact microbench command you used so I can repro locally?
alex: Sure — command I used:
```
kbench --model llama2 --seq-len 512 --batch-size 1 --kernel v3.2-cand --iter 1000 --profile /tmp/trace.json
```
jamie: Hmm, the numbers look like the selector picked an AVX512 path on ampere. That would be wrong — ampere shouldn't hit avx512 variants. :eyes:
marco: On Ampere we expect avx2/tensorcore kernels. If autotune metadata has stale arch tags we could be selecting the wrong kernel variant.
nina: Also worth checking KV cache behavior — I saw a similar tail previously where KV refill caused memcpy spikes at the start of generation.
alex: Perf summary from the trace (excerpt):
```
median: base=3.8ms cand=3.9ms (+2.6%)
p95:   base=6.4ms cand=6.9ms (+7.8%)
p99:   base=12.3ms cand=13.8ms (+12.2%)
notes: cpu memcpy spikes aligned with KV refill events at step 1
```
priya: OK assigning triage: @jamie you take kernel-selector, @marco take autotune ingestion/artifacts, @nina you look at KV cache traces + batcher interaction. Ping if you need creds.
jamie: I'll repro with the uploaded repro. Alex — can you confirm repro.zip contains the full env + docker tag?
alex: Uploaded repro and syscall trace at https://ci.redwood.prod/jobs/548/repro.zip — includes docker: redwood/kbench:v2026-05-01 and a minimal dataset.
marco: I queried the autotune DB for v3.2-cand entries: meta.arch_tag=ampere but flags include avx512:true. Looks like builder didn't clear legacy arch flags during packaging. :facepalm:
jamie: That would explain the handshake choosing avx512 kernels. Quick mitigation: kernel-selector should ignore avx512 flag unless hw_arch strictly matches x86_64_avx512.
nina: KV logs show a miss storm when batcher coalesced multiple 512 requests that had different prefix states — KV refill happened repeatedly. Adding a tiny cooldown between coalesced batches reduced miss rate in local run.
priya: For CI gating — what are we using as regression thresholds today? I remember p95 <=5% and p99 <=8% as soft gates.
alex: Historically yes. Proposal: keep numeric thresholds but add flaky-run detection: require regression to be observed in 3 consecutive sweeps before blocking a candidate. Also tag regressions by root cause (selector vs kv vs kernel correctness).
jamie: I'll open a draft PR to make kernel-selector stricter about arch tags. PR #342 (draft) — patch to refuse avx512 variant selection on ampere unless explicit hw_capability present. :memo:
ci-bot: PR #342 created by jamie. microbench smoke passed. scheduling full kbench-autotune run.
marco: I'll add a sanitizer on ingest to strip incompatible arch flags and emit a warning so builders don't silently ship bad metadata.
nina: I'll prototype a KV cooldown backoff in the batcher — thinking 8ms cooldown for matched seq_len coalesces; it cut miss storms in my local simulation by ~60%.
priya: Great. Can we capture acceptance criteria and owners in a tracking issue so QA can re-run sweeps after fixes?
alex: Created INF-1273 with plan, owners, and links to CI artifacts: https://go.redwood/INF-1273 :link:
jamie: After #342 lands I'll run a targeted sweep for seq_len=512 on ampere pools and post updated metrics. Expect results within 2 runs (~overnight).
priya: Sounds good. If any of you hit flaky CI noise, mark the job as non-blocking and put details in INF-1273. We don't want single-sweep flakiness to block deploys. :thumbsup:
marco: Follow-ups: autobuilder change, selector patch, autotune-ingest guard. I'll create small PRs and link from the issue.
nina: I'll open a small eval that exercises KV cooldown across batcher permutations.
alex: Awesome, thanks all. Keeping this thread for updates — please ping here when you have diffs/links. :rocket:
